story.title: The Last Lantern
story.premise: When the island's last lantern goes dark, a reluctant keeper must choose who to trust.
story.thematic_statement: Trust is a light people keep together.

character.name: Maya
character.misbelief: Depending on anyone means losing them.

character.name: Eli
character.want: Tell Maya what happened at the harbor
character.need: Face his part in the secret

location.name: Lighthouse
location.description: The island's last working lantern overlooks a reef.

location.name: Harbor
location.description: A stone quay where the sea keeps an old secret.

scene.title: The lantern goes out
scene.summary: Maya's lantern goes dark. Eli offers help, and she reluctantly lets him in.
scene.conflict: The mechanism fails in a storm
scene.outcome: Maya opens the door to Eli
scene.content:
Maya counted the steps to the lantern room every night. Forty-seven from the kitchen, twelve more after the landing where the wind pressed its fingers through the wall. She knew which boards complained. She knew where to put her hand when the sea turned the tower cold. If she kept counting, there was no room to remember the last person who had climbed these stairs beside her.

At the top she trimmed the wick, polished the glass, and checked the brass wheel that turned the lantern toward the reef. Outside, three fishing boats were coming home. Their small lights rose and vanished between the waves. Maya watched until she had counted all three again. The island could sleep while she stayed awake. That was the arrangement. It had always seemed fair.

Then the wheel stopped. No warning, no slowing tick. The light held still against the rain, a pale hand stretched toward nothing. Maya reached for the handle. It burned her palm. Beneath the floor, something struck the tower once, hard enough to shake dust from the stairs. The wick gave a little blue gasp and went out.

Darkness filled the glass. She tried the spare matches, shielding them inside her coat, but the first snapped and the second hissed against the damp wick. Through the window she could no longer find the boats. The reef was a black line hidden inside a black sea. Maya pushed the handle again. The wheel would not move.

Someone knocked downstairs. She knew the rhythm: two quick blows, a pause, then one more. Eli had knocked like that when they were children, when he wanted her to come down to the harbor and see something he had found. She had not answered his knocking for seven years. Tonight it sounded very far away.

She took the broken match to the stairwell. A voice came up through the dark. 'Maya? I saw the light stop.' She could tell him to go home. She could say the tower was hers to mend. Both sentences were waiting, familiar and easy, while somewhere beyond the window a boat was moving toward the reef.

'Bring the rope,' she said. She heard herself before she understood what she had done. The door opened, and a cold gust brought the smell of salt and wet wool into the tower. Eli's boots sounded on the first stair. Maya set the match down and made room beside the wheel.

scene.title: A secret beneath the harbor
scene.summary: Maya remembers the harbor secret from seven years earlier; readers discover it after the lantern fails.
scene.content:
Seven years earlier, the harbor had been quiet enough for Maya to hear the rope scrape along the quay. Eli stood at the water's edge with a brass box under his coat. He would not tell her where it had come from, only that a trader in [TK: name of the mainland port] had sold it cheap. He only said that some things were better left in the sea.

She remembered the yellow lantern above the harbor gate. A moth circled it, landing each time on the same pane. Her father had told her that the light belonged to everyone, even the people who could not see it from home. That night she had understood him to mean the boats. Now, in the dark tower, she wondered whether he had meant the people on shore.

Eli lowered the box over the edge. It struck the water without a splash she could hear. 'You mustn't tell,' he said. Maya promised because she trusted him. By morning her father was gone, the harbor lantern was broken, and trust had become a word she could no longer say without thinking of the sea.

The memory ended where it always ended: Eli's empty hands and the rope sinking after the box. But tonight there was a detail she had never let herself notice. His hands had been shaking. He had been a child, too.

scene.title: Keep the light together
scene.summary: Maya and Eli mend the lantern together.
scene.content:
Eli held the rope while Maia climbed into the housing of the wheel. The broken pin was smaller than her thumb. She had spent seven years imagining that anything capable of stopping the light would have to be enormous.

'I can hold it,' Eli said. She looked down. He had looped the rope twice around his hands, the way her father used to. For a moment she was back at the harbor. Then she was here, and the tower was cold, and someone was waiting for her answer.

'All right.' She passed him the weight and felt it leave her shoulders. Together they turned the wheel. The wick caught on the first match this time. Light swept across the reef, and far below them a fishing boat sounded its horn.

When the sun came up, Maya did not count the stairs. She and Eli carried the broken pin down between them. At the kitchen door she stopped, found two cups, and put the kettle on.
